s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bilateral lower limb weakness and pain with signs of inflammation and nerve paralysis following unaccustomed physical activity
key_facts: Unipolar major depression with psychotic features
Completed a 5 km flat walk the evening prior to symptom onset
Presented to the emergency department three days later
Visibly swollen and reddish colored legs

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bilateral lower limb weakness and pain with signs of inflammation and nerve paralysis following unaccustomed physical activity
key_facts: Unipolar major depression with psychotic features
Completed a 5 km flat walk the evening prior to symptom onset
Presented to the emergency department three days later
Visibly swollen and reddish colored legs

shortlist.label: Compartment syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral peroneal nerve paralysis, hardened painful forelegs, and visibly swollen legs suggest increased pressure within the muscle compartments

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CPK levels (15,000U/L) and muscle edema on MRI indicate muscle damage and necrosis

shortlist.label: Exertional myositis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent unaccustomed physical activity (5 km walk) and muscle edema on MRI support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of necrosis in tibialis anterior muscles on MRI and signs of inflammation (CRP: 280mg/dL, WBC: 25,000/μL) make this a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Hardened painful forelegs and visibly swollen legs, along with elevated inflammatory markers, could be indicative of this condition

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of bilateral foot drop, painful swelling of the legs, hardened painful forelegs, and visibly swollen and reddish colored legs, along with the laboratory findings of elevated CPK and imaging studies showing indirect signs of myositis and panniculitis, are consistent with compartment syndrome. The recent unusual physical exertion of a 5 km walk may have triggered the condition.

rejected.label: Rhabdomyolysis
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated CPK, the presence of bilateral peroneal nerve paralysis and the imaging findings suggest a more localized process like compartment syndrome rather than the diffuse muscle damage seen in rhabdomyolysis.

rejected.label: Exertional myositis
rejected.why: Exertional myositis typically presents with muscle pain and stiffness after exercise, but it does not usually cause the severe swelling, nerve paralysis, and compartmental signs seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
rejected.why: Necrotizing fasciitis is a severe infection that would likely present with a higher fever, more pronounced systemic signs of infection, and gas in the soft tissues on imaging, which are not described in this case.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
rejected.why: Eosinophilic fasciitis is characterized by thickening of the skin and fascia, but it does not typically cause acute nerve paralysis or the degree of swelling and pain seen in this patient.
